mainTopic: Which brother does חליצה, whether יבום or חליצה comes first, and the מחלוקת of אבא שאול and the רבנן about intention in יבום.
overview: The גמרא first brings a second version of the מחלוקת between רבי יוחנן and רבי יהושע בן לוי. In this version, everyone agrees that יבום by a younger brother beats חליצה by the eldest, and they argue only whether the eldest's חליצה is better than a younger brother's. Proofs from the משנה are tried on both sides, but each is pushed off; the court's refusal to wait is explained by the rule that we do not delay a מצוה. Next, a משנה teaches that once יבום came first, but now that people lack pure intentions, חליצה comes first. רב rules that the court does not force a יבם to do חליצה, and רב יהודה's חליצה document shows he agreed; the גמרא also rules that identifying the brother is only גלויי מילתא, so even a relative or a woman is believed. רמי בר חמא reports that later they went back to putting יבום first, and the גמרא explains this as a switch from אבא שאול's view to the רבנן's view. Finally, the גמרא asks which תנא taught a ברייתא calling יבום a 'מצוה'. רבי יצחק בר אבדימי says it is אבא שאול, and רבא reads it to fit the רבנן. The גמרא then starts testing these readings against the ברייתא's first clause about מנחות, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A second version: everyone agrees about consummation
steps.stepSummary: A different version of the מחלוקת: all agree that ביאה by a younger brother is better than the eldest's חליצה; the argument is only about a younger brother's חליצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: about ביאה (doing יבום), everyone agrees that a younger brother's ביאה is better. They argue only about a younger brother's חליצה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a second version of the earlier argument and makes it narrower. It sets up the new wording of the מחלוקת that comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the earlier version, the argument was whether a younger brother's יבום beats the eldest's חליצה. This version takes that off the table: everyone agrees יבום by a younger brother wins. The only open question is a younger brother's חליצה compared to the eldest's חליצה.

keyTerms.meaning: There are those who say: introduces a second version of a teaching
Everyone agrees (literally: the whole world does not argue)
Here: a younger brother, not a minor

steps.confusionAlert: Here קטן means a younger brother, not a child below בר מצוה. גדול means the eldest brother.

phrases.english: There are those who say:
Regarding consummation, everyone agrees
phrases.notes: Here this means doing יבום, actually marrying the widow, rather than חליצה.

phrases.english: that consummation by a younger brother is preferable.
Where they disagree is about the חליצה of a younger brother.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Presents a second version of the מחלוקת discussed just before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All agree a younger brother's יבום beats the eldest's חליצה; the argument is only about a younger brother's חליצה.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן and רבי יהושע בן לוי argue about younger vs. eldest חליצה
steps.stepSummary: The מחלוקת in this version: one says the eldest's חליצה is preferable, the other says the two are equal.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is how it was taught: about a younger brother's חליצה versus the eldest's חליצה, רבי יוחנן and רבי יהושע בן לוי argue. One says the eldest's חליצה is better, and one says they are equal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states the exact wording of the argument in this second version.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both opinions agree that a younger brother's חליצה works. The only question is whether the eldest brother should be preferred, or whether any brother is just as good. The גמרא does not say which אמורא holds which view.

keyTerms.meaning: It was stated: introduces a teaching of the אמוראים
The ceremony that releases the widow from יבום
They are equal to each other

phrases.english: And this is how it was stated:
The חליצה of a younger brother and the חליצה of the eldest:

phrases.aramaic: פְּלִיגִי בַּהּ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי.
phrases.english: רבי יוחנן and רבי יהושע בן לוי disagree about it.
One said: the eldest's חליצה is preferable,
and the other said: they are equal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the full wording of the narrower מחלוקת introduced in step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One view: the eldest's חליצה is preferable. Other view: the eldest's and a younger brother's חליצה are equal.

steps.title: Reason for preferring the eldest: the מצוה is on him
steps.stepSummary: The view that prefers the eldest's חליצה is based on the rule 'מצוה בגדול'.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who says the eldest's חליצה is better holds so because the מצוה belongs to the eldest brother.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reasoning of the first opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a known rule that the מצוה of יבום falls first on the eldest brother. This opinion stretches that rule to cover חליצה too, so the eldest is preferred for חליצה as well.

keyTerms.meaning: The one who said: introduces the reason of one opinion
The מצוה is on the eldest brother

phrases.english: The one who said the eldest's חליצה is preferable:
this is because the מצוה is upon the eldest.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning of the first opinion in step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The eldest's חליצה is preferable because of the principle מצוה בגדול.

steps.title: The other view: 'the מצוה is on the eldest' applies only to יבום
steps.stepSummary: The second opinion limits the rule 'מצוה בגדול' to יבום; for חליצה, all brothers are equal.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other opinion? When we say the מצוה is on the eldest, that is about יבום. But about חליצה, they are all equal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how the second opinion answers the first opinion's reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The second opinion accepts the rule 'מצוה בגדול' but says it only covers יבום. חליצה is not included, so no brother has an advantage. This is why he says the two are equal.

keyTerms.meaning: And the other one: how does the other opinion respond?
Levirate marriage: the brother marries his late brother's widow

steps.whatToRemember: Both sides accept 'מצוה בגדול'. The argument is only whether the rule covers חליצה or only יבום.

phrases.english: And the other one?

phrases.aramaic: כִּי אָמְרִינַן מִצְוָה בַּגָּדוֹל לְעִנְיַן יִבּוּם,
phrases.english: When we say the מצוה is upon the eldest, that is with regard to יבום,
but with regard to חליצה,
they are equal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the principle used as the reason in step 3.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects applying the principle מצוה בגדול to חליצה, not the principle itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The first opinion stretches a rule about יבום to cover חליצה.

steps.title: Proof from the משנה: they go back to the eldest for חליצה
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says that if the younger brothers refuse, the court goes back to the eldest. This suggests the eldest's חליצה is preferred even when younger brothers are willing to do חליצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in the משנה: if they did not want to, the court goes back to the eldest. Doesn't this mean they did not want to do יבום, but were willing to do חליצה? And still the משנה says to go back to the eldest. So learn from this that the eldest's חליצה is better!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to prove from a משנה that the eldest's חליצה is preferable, which challenges the opinion that all brothers are equal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא reads 'they did not want' as: the younger brothers refused only יבום but were ready to do חליצה. If all brothers were equal for חליצה, a younger brother could just do it. Since the משנה sends the case back to the eldest, it seems his חליצה is preferred.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it not that...? Introduces a suggested reading
Learn from it: draws a conclusion

steps.confusionAlert: The proof depends on reading 'לא רצו' as refusing only יבום. If it meant refusing everything, there would be no proof.

phrases.english: We learned: If they did not want,
phrases.notes: This is from our משנה, where the eldest is asked first. 'They' means the younger brothers.

phrases.english: they go back to the eldest.
Is it not that they did not want to do יבום,
but they were willing to do חליצה?
And it teaches: they go back to the eldest,
so learn from it that the eldest's חליצה is preferable!

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן: לֹא רָצוּ חוֹזְרִין אֵצֶל גָּדוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source to support the first opinion against the 'equal' view of step 4.
steps.raayaObject: The opinion that the eldest's חליצה is preferable.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה: 'לא רצו חוזרין אצל גדול', read as the younger brothers refusing only יבום.

steps.title: The younger brothers refused both options
steps.stepSummary: The proof is rejected. The משנה may be talking about younger brothers who refused both יבום and חליצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. The case is where the younger brothers wanted neither to do חליצה nor to do יבום.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof from Step 5. The משנה might be describing younger brothers who refused everything, not brothers who were willing to do חליצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof assumed that the younger brothers were willing to do חליצה and the court still went back to the eldest. The גמרא now reads the case differently: they refused both options. If so, going back to the eldest says nothing about which brother's חליצה is better.

phrases.english: No, [the case is where] they did not want
either to perform חליצה or to do יבום,

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, לֹא רָצוּ לֹא לַחְלוֹץ וְלָא לְיַיבֵּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of Step 5 by redefining the case in the משנה.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof that the eldest's חליצה is preferred over a younger brother's willing חליצה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed that the younger brothers were willing to do חליצה. They may have refused both options.

steps.title: Then why bother going back to the eldest?
steps.stepSummary: If the eldest also refused both options, why does the court go back to him instead of forcing the younger brothers?
steps.simpleTranslation: The same would apply to the eldest: he refused both חליצה and יבום. If so, why go back to the eldest to force him? Let the court force the younger ones!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the new reading from Step 6. If everyone refused, why go back to the eldest at all?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה uses the same words, "did not want," for the eldest. So he too refused both options. If all the brothers are equally refusing, the court could simply force a younger brother who is right there. Going back to the eldest seems like wasted effort.

keyTerms.meaning: we go back to the eldest

phrases.english: Similarly, regarding the eldest:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא רָצָה לֹא לַחְלוֹץ וְלֹא לְיַיבֵּם.
phrases.english: he did not want either to do חליצה or to do יבום.
But then why do we go back to the eldest
to force him? Let us force them!
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the word in round brackets; the word in square brackets is the corrected wording, "let us force them."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the case definition offered in Step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that the younger brothers refused both יבום and חליצה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If every brother refused, there is no reason to prefer forcing the eldest over forcing a younger brother who is present.

steps.title: The מצוה rests on the eldest first
steps.stepSummary: Because the מצוה is placed on the eldest first, he is the one the court forces.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since the מצוה rests on him first, he is the one we force.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The eldest is the one forced because the מצוה was his to begin with.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even when every brother refuses, the eldest has the first obligation (based on "מצוה בגדול"). So when force is needed, the court turns to him. This does not prove that his חליצה is better than a younger brother's willing חליצה.

phrases.english: Since the מצוה rests on him,
phrases.notes: "Him" is the eldest brother, who has the first obligation.

phrases.english: it is him we force.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 7, so the rejection in Step 6 stands.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains that the eldest is singled out for forcing, not for having a better חליצה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If all the brothers refuse, there is no reason to go back to the eldest.
steps.terutzMaskana: The obligation falls on the eldest first, so he is the one the court forces.

steps.title: We do not wait for the eldest who is overseas
steps.stepSummary: A new proof that all brothers are equal for חליצה. The court does not wait for an eldest brother who is overseas.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: if a brother made it depend on the eldest, saying to wait until he returns from overseas, the court does not listen to him. If the eldest's חליצה were better, why not listen? Let the court wait, since perhaps he will come and do חליצה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another line from the משנה to prove that the eldest's חליצה is not better than a younger brother's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the eldest's חליצה were truly preferred, it would make sense to wait for him to come back. Since the משנה refuses to wait, it seems that a younger brother's חליצה is just as good.

keyTerms.meaning: we do not listen to him

phrases.english: Come and hear:
If he made it depend on the eldest,
phrases.notes: "He" is a younger brother who wants to push off the decision.

phrases.english: until he comes back from overseas,
we do not listen to him.
And if you think
that the eldest's חליצה is better,
why do we not listen to him?
Let us wait, since perhaps he will come and do חליצה!

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: תָּלָה בַּגָּדוֹל עַד שֶׁיָּבֹא מִמְּדִינַת הַיָּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the proof for the first view was rejected, the גמרא brings a proof for the second view.
steps.raayaObject: The view that all brothers are equal for חליצה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's ruling that we do not wait for the eldest who is overseas.

steps.title: Your logic would also force waiting for a minor
steps.stepSummary: The proof is pushed back. By the same logic, the court should wait for a minor brother to grow up so he can do יבום, yet it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: And by your reasoning: when the eldest asks to wait until a minor brother grows up, we do not listen to him. Why not? Let us wait, since perhaps the minor will grow up and do יבום. (Or: perhaps the eldest will come back and do יבום with her.)
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the proof from Step 9 goes too far. Everyone agrees יבום is better, yet the משנה still refuses to wait for it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If refusing to wait proved that the eldest's חליצה is not better, then refusing to wait for a minor would prove that יבום is not better, and that is impossible. So refusing to wait must have some other reason. The proof from Step 9 falls apart.

phrases.english: And by your reasoning: with a minor, [waiting] until he grows up,
we do not listen to him. Why?
Let us wait, since perhaps he will grow up and do יבום.
(Or else: he will come back and do יבום with her.)
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out these words in round brackets. "He" here would be the eldest who is overseas.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of Step 9 by showing that its logic leads to an impossible result.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the inference from "we do not wait" to "the eldest's חליצה is not better."
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The same reasoning would prove that יבום is not better than חליצה, which nobody accepts.

steps.title: We do not delay a מצוה
steps.stepSummary: The real reason we do not wait is that we never put off doing a מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: we never delay a מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the true reason behind the משנה's refusal to wait. We do not hold up a מצוה that can be done now.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's refusal to wait has nothing to do with which brother's חליצה is better. It comes from a separate rule: a מצוה that can be done now should not be pushed off. So the question from Steps 2-4 stays unresolved.
steps.whatToRemember: The court does not wait for an absent or underage brother because we never delay a מצוה. So neither proof settles whether the eldest's חליצה is better.
steps.whyThisMatters: "We do not delay a מצוה" is a general principle that explains the משנה's rulings without deciding the מחלוקת.

phrases.english: Rather: any delaying of a מצוה,
we do not delay.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: כֹּל שַׁהוֹיֵי מִצְוָה לָא מְשַׁהֵינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the rejection of Step 10 by stating the real reason for the משנה's ruling.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The משנה refuses to wait because we do not delay a מצוה, not because all brothers are equal for חליצה.

steps.title: Which comes first: יבום or חליצה
steps.stepSummary: A new topic opens with a משנה. Originally יבום came before חליצה, but now that people lack pure intentions, חליצה comes first.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned there: the מצוה of יבום comes before the מצוה of חליצה. That was in earlier times, when people intended to do it for the sake of the מצוה. Now that they do not intend it for the sake of the מצוה, the חכמים said: the מצוה of חליצה comes before the מצוה of יבום.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new section by quoting a משנה from another מסכת about whether יבום or חליצה is preferred.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says the ranking changed over time. יבום was first when brothers did it purely for the מצוה. Once people started marrying the יבמה for other reasons, such as her beauty or money, the חכמים put חליצה first. This sets up the discussion that follows.

keyTerms.meaning: we learned there (in a משנה elsewhere)
for the sake of the מצוה

steps.confusionAlert: This is not saying the Torah changed. The חכמים changed which option is preferred because people's intentions changed.

phrases.english: We learned there:
The mitzvah of יבום comes before the mitzvah of חליצה.
That was in earlier times, when they intended it for the sake of the מצוה.
Now that they do not intend it for the sake of the מצוה,

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ: מִצְוַת חֲלִיצָה קוֹדֶמֶת לְמִצְוַת יִבּוּם.
phrases.english: they said: the mitzvah of חליצה comes before the mitzvah of יבום.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן הָתָם: מִצְוַת יִבּוּם קוֹדֶמֶת לְמִצְוַת חֲלִיצָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new section unrelated to the eldest-brother question.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Originally יבום took priority. Now, because intentions are not pure, חליצה takes priority.

steps.title: רב: the court does not force חליצה
steps.stepSummary: רב rules that even though חליצה is preferred, the court does not force the יבם. He may choose either חליצה or יבום, based on the פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: We do not force him. When a case came before רב, he would tell them: If you want, do חליצה. If you want, do יבום. The Torah left it up to you. It says 'And if the man does not want…', which means that if he does want, he may choose either one.
steps.whatsHappening: רב adds a limit to the משנה's rule that חליצה comes first: the court will not force the יבם to do חליצה. He backs this up with a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said חליצה is now preferred, but that is only advice, not something the court enforces. רב reads 'if the man does not want' to mean the Torah left the choice to the יבם. So if he wants יבום, he may still do it.

keyTerms.meaning: We do not force (the court does not compel him)
Do חליצה (release her by removing the shoe)
The Torah made it depend on you

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with the משנה. The משנה says חליצה is preferred nowadays. רב says the court will not force the יבם to do חליצה. He may choose either one.

phrases.english: Rav said: We do not force him.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי אֲתוֹ לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב, אֲמַר לְהוּ:
phrases.english: When they came before Rav, he said to them:
phrases.notes: 'They' means a יבם and a יבמה who came to court.

phrases.aramaic: אִי בָּעֵית — חֲלוֹץ, אִי בָּעֵית — יַיבֵּם.
phrases.english: If you want, do חליצה; if you want, do יבום.
The Merciful One made it depend on you:
"And if the man does not want"
This implies that if he does want,

phrases.aramaic: אִי בָּעֵי — חָלֵיץ, אִי בָּעֵי — יְיַבֵּם.
phrases.english: if he wants he does חליצה, and if he wants he does יבום.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the משנה's preference for חליצה: the preference is not enforced by the court.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The court does not force a יבם to do חליצה. He may choose יבום or חליצה, because the Torah left the choice to him.

steps.title: רב יהודה agrees, as his חליצה document shows
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proves that רב יהודה also held that we do not force, because the חליצה document he set up tells the יבם he may do יבום if he wants.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה also held that we do not force him. We know this because he set up the wording of the חליצה document: 'So-and-so, daughter of so-and-so, brought so-and-so, her יבם, before us in court. We checked and found that he is the brother of the dead man from the same father. We said to him: If you want to do יבום, do יבום. If not, lift your right foot to her.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that רב יהודה agrees with רב. The proof comes from the official wording he set for the חליצה document.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the document, the court tells the יבם, 'If you want to do יבום, do יבום.' A court that forced חליצה would never offer that choice. So the wording itself shows that רב יהודה held אין כופין.

keyTerms.meaning: The חליצה document written by the court
So-and-so, daughter of so-and-so (a placeholder for real names)
We identified him, we checked who he was

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף רַב יְהוּדָה סָבַר אֵין כּוֹפִין.
phrases.english: And Rav Yehuda also holds that we do not force.
Since Rav Yehuda set up the wording of the חליצה document:
That so-and-so, daughter of so-and-so,
phrases.notes: אֵיךְ here is just the opening word of the document, meaning 'that', not 'how'.

phrases.english: brought so-and-so, her יבם,
before us in court,
and we identified him as the brother of the dead man from the father,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לֵיהּ: אִי צָבֵית לְיַבֵּם — יַבֵּם,
phrases.english: and we said to him: If you want to do יבום, do יבום,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי לָא — אַיטְלַע לַהּ רִגְלָיךְ דְּיַמִּינָא.
phrases.english: and if not, lift your right foot to her.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַף רַב יְהוּדָה סָבַר אֵין כּוֹפִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב's ruling by showing that רב יהודה held the same view.
steps.raayaObject: That רב יהודה also held אין כופין
steps.raayaSupportSource: The wording of רב יהודה's חליצה document, which offers the יבם the choice of יבום

steps.title: The rest of the document: how the חליצה was done
steps.stepSummary: The document goes on to record what happened: he lifted his right foot, she took off his shoe, and she spat in front of him onto the ground where the court could see it.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And he lifted his right foot to her, and she took his shoe off his foot, and she spat in front of his face spit that the court could see, onto the ground.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps quoting רב יהודה's document. This part records the actual steps of the חליצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This part does not add to the proof. It finishes the document by describing the חליצה itself. Notice the spit lands on the ground in front of him, and the court must be able to see it.

phrases.english: And he lifted his right foot to her,
and she took his shoe off his foot,
and she spat in front of his face

phrases.aramaic: רוּקָּא דְּמִתְחַזְיָא לְבֵי דִינָא עַל אַרְעָא.
phrases.english: spit that the court could see, onto the ground.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues quoting the same document from the previous step.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The חליצה document records the removal of the right shoe and spit that the court can see, landing on the ground.

steps.title: The closing line of the document
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר אויא, quoting רב יהודה, ends the document with one more line: the court had them read out the words written in the Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אויא ended it, in the name of רב יהודה, like this: 'And we had them read what is written in the book of the Torah of משה.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final line of רב יהודה's document, as quoted by רבי חייא בר אויא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Besides the actions, חליצה also needs the spoken words from the Torah. This last line records that the court had them say those words, so the document covers every part of the חליצה.

keyTerms.meaning: He ends it with, he adds a closing line
We had them read, we read it out to them

steps.whatToRemember: The court does not force a יבם to do חליצה (רב, and רב יהודה agrees). רב יהודה's חליצה document offers him the choice of יבום, records the shoe removal and the spit, and ends by noting that the Torah's words were read out.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַוְיָא מְסַיֵּים בַּהּ מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוּדָה:
phrases.english: And Rabbi Chiyya bar Avya ends it in the name of Rav Yehuda:
And we had them read what is written
in the book of the Torah of Moshe.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַוְיָא מְסַיֵּים בַּהּ מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the final sentence to the document quoted in the previous two steps.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The חליצה document ends by noting that the court had them read the Torah's words.

steps.title: How do we identify the brother? Two opinions
steps.stepSummary: The document says 'we identified him' as the brother. רב אחא and רבינא argue over how that identification must be made: through proper witnesses, or even through a relative or a woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And we identified him': רב אחא and רבינא disagree about this. One says it needs proper witnesses. The other says even a relative, even a woman, is enough.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא picks up a phrase from רב יהודה's חליצה document, 'we identified him.' It brings a disagreement about who is allowed to confirm that this man is really the brother.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The court has to know the man doing חליצה is truly the dead husband's brother. One opinion treats this like formal testimony, which needs kosher עדים. The other opinion says it is less strict, so even people who normally cannot testify, like a relative or a woman, are believed.

keyTerms.meaning: We identified him / we recognized him
A relative, normally not allowed to testify

phrases.english: "And we identified him":
phrases.notes: This phrase comes from רב יהודה's חליצה document in step 14. The court confirms this man really is the dead man's brother.

phrases.english: Rav Aḥa and Ravina disagree about it.
One said: through witnesses.

phrases.aramaic: וְחַד אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ קָרוֹב, אֲפִילּוּ אִשָּׁה.
phrases.english: And one said: even a relative, even a woman.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִשְׁתְּמוֹדְעִינְהוּ, פְּלִיגִי בַּהּ רַב אַחָא וְרָבִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to explain a phrase in the חליצה document whose wording was recorded in the earlier steps.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is a disagreement: one says the identification needs proper witnesses, the other says even a relative or a woman is believed.

steps.title: The הלכה: identifying the brother is just revealing a fact
steps.stepSummary: The הלכה follows the lenient view. Identifying the brother is only making a fact known, so even a relative or a woman is believed.
steps.simpleTranslation: The הלכה is: it is just revealing the matter, so even a relative and even a woman are believed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא decides the argument from the last step and sides with the lenient opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason is that identifying the brother is not real testimony. It is only 'revealing the matter,' showing a fact that is not truly in doubt. Since this is not formal testimony, the strict rules for who may testify do not apply.

keyTerms.meaning: Revealing a matter, just making a fact known, not formal testimony

steps.whatToRemember: Identifying the יבם is only גלויי מילתא, so even a relative or a woman is believed.
steps.whyThisMatters: The idea of גלויי מילתא, a fact that only needs to be revealed and not formally proven, comes up in many places. It explains why the usual rules for עדים sometimes do not apply.

phrases.english: And the halacha is: it is merely revealing the matter,
and even a relative and even a woman are believed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides the disagreement brought in step 17.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Identifying the brother is only revealing a fact, so a relative or a woman may do it.

steps.title: The rule restated: when יבום came first and when חליצה came first
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה again. When people meant it for the sake of the מצוה‎, יבום came first. Now that they do not, חליצה comes first.
steps.simpleTranslation: At first, when people meant it for the sake of the מצוה, the מצוה of יבום came before the מצוה of חליצה. Now that they do not mean it for the sake of the מצוה, they said: the מצוה of חליצה comes before the מצוה of יבום.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats the rule about which מצוה comes first. It does this to set up the next move, a later report that the rule changed back again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This line was already learned in step 12. The גמרא brings it again here as the base for רמי בר חמא's statement. The key point is that putting חליצה first depends on people's intentions.

keyTerms.meaning: For the sake of the מצוה

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new opinion. It is the same rule from the משנה in step 12, repeated so the גמרא can build on it.

phrases.english: At first, when they would intend it for the sake of the מצוה,
the mitzvah of יבום came before the mitzvah of חליצה.
And now that they do not intend it for the sake of the מצוה,

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ: מִצְוַת חֲלִיצָה קוֹדֶמֶת לְמִצְוַת יִבּוּם.
phrases.english: they said: the mitzvah of חליצה comes before the mitzvah of יבום.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the document discussion and goes back to the משנה from step 12, as a setup for the next statement.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Today, because people lack pure intentions, חליצה comes before יבום.

steps.title: Later they went back to putting יבום first
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא, quoting רבי יצחק, reports that later the rule was changed back: יבום again comes before חליצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר חמא said in the name of רבי יצחק: They went back and said that the מצוה of יבום comes before the מצוה of חליצה.
steps.whatsHappening: A new statement says the rule from the משנה was reversed again, so יבום is once more first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה linked putting חליצה first to people's poor intentions. So a change back to יבום first seems to suggest something about people changed. That puzzle sets up the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: They went back and said (they reversed the ruling)
An אמורא who reports רבי יצחק's teaching

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רָמֵי בַּר חָמָא אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק:
phrases.english: Rami bar Ḥama said that Rabbi Yitzḥak said:
They went back to saying
that the mitzvah of יבום comes before the mitzvah of חליצה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָמֵי בַּר חָמָא אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק: חָזְרוּ לוֹמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reports that the rule just repeated in step 19 was later reversed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the end, יבום again comes before חליצה.

steps.title: Did the generations get better?
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק asks in surprise: did the later generations improve so much that they now act purely for the מצוה?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said to him: Did the generations become better?
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק challenges רמי בר חמא's report. It seems impossible that people's intentions improved.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said חליצה comes first because people no longer act for the sake of the מצוה. If יבום is first again, that would mean people became pure again. This is hard to believe, so the report seems not to make sense.

keyTerms.meaning: Did the generations become better (more kosher)?

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק:
phrases.english: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said to him:
Did the generations improve?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: אִכַּשּׁוּר דָּרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the report in step 20 using the reason given in step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: רמי בר חמא's report that יבום went back to being first.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If חליצה came first because of bad intentions, then putting יבום first again means intentions improved, and that is not believable.

steps.title: The change came from switching opinions, not from better people
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the generations did not improve. At first they followed אבא שאול, who puts חליצה first. Later they followed the רבנן, who put יבום first.
steps.simpleTranslation: At first they held like אבא שאול, and in the end they held like the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רב נחמן בר יצחק's challenge. The change was about which opinion to follow, not about people becoming better.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule that חליצה comes first matches the view of אבא שאול. Later, the ruling followed the רבנן, who say יבום comes first anyway. So the reversal was a change in which opinion the הלכה follows, and it says nothing about people's intentions.

keyTerms.meaning: They held like (followed the opinion of)
A תנא who is strict against יבום not done for the מצוה

steps.whatToRemember: The ruling that יבום comes first again does not mean people improved. It means the הלכה moved from אבא שאול's view to the רבנן's view.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how a practical rule can change because the ruling switched from one opinion to another, not because the facts on the ground changed.

phrases.english: At first they held like Abba Shaul,
and in the end they held like the Rabbis.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵעִיקָּרָא סָבְרִי לַהּ כְּאַבָּא שָׁאוּל, וּלְבַסּוֹף סָבְרִי לַהּ כְּרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Changes the reason for the reversal: it was a shift in which opinion to follow, not a change in people.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The return to יבום first meant the generations had become purer in their intentions.
steps.terutzMaskana: The return to יבום first happened because the halacha moved from אבא שאול's view to the רבנן's view.

steps.title: אבא שאול: Marrying a יבמה for the wrong reason is like an ערוה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that אבא שאול holds that יבום done for beauty, for married life, or for any other reason is like being with a forbidden relative, and the child may even be a ממזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: אבא שאול says, someone who marries his יבמה for her beauty, for married life, or for any other reason, it is as if he touched an ערוה. I am close to saying that the child is a ממזר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא as the source for step 22, which said the earlier generations followed אבא שאול. This step gives אבא שאול's side of the מחלוקת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A brother's wife is normally an ערוה. The Torah lifts that איסור only for the מצוה of יבום. So אבא שאול says that without the מצוה in mind, the איסור is back in force. He is so strict that he leans toward calling the child a ממזר.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא who holds that יבום must be done only for the sake of the מצוה
His יבמה: the widow of his brother who died without children
For the sake of her beauty
For the sake of married life
Touches (has relations with) a forbidden relative
A child born from a forbidden relationship

steps.confusionAlert: אבא שאול does not say outright that it is an ערוה. He says it is LIKE an ערוה, and that he is only 'close' to calling the child a ממזר. That is very strong language, but it is said carefully.

phrases.english: As it is taught in a ברייתא: אבא שאול says:
One who marries his יבמה for the sake of her beauty,
or for the sake of married life, or for the sake of something else,
it is as though he came upon a forbidden relative.

phrases.aramaic: וְקָרוֹב אֲנִי בְּעֵינַי לִהְיוֹת הַוָּלָד מַמְזֵר.
phrases.english: And I am inclined in my eyes to consider the child a ממזר.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the ברייתא behind step 22's claim that the earlier generations followed אבא שאול.
steps.raayaObject: The claim in step 22 that אבא שאול requires יבום only for the מצוה, so חליצה is preferred

steps.title: The חכמים: יבום is valid whatever the reason
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים disagree with אבא שאול. The פסוק 'her יבם shall come upon her' means יבום is proper in any case.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים say: 'Her יבם shall come upon her' — in any case.
steps.whatsHappening: The same ברייתא now gives the other side of the מחלוקת: the חכמים, who are the רבנן the later generations followed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים read the פסוק as a general instruction with no condition about his reason. So even if he marries her for beauty or for married life, he has done יבום properly. That is why the later generations could put יבום before חליצה.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages, the majority view (the רבנן of step 22)
'Her brother-in-law shall come upon her' — the פסוק commanding יבום
In any case, no matter what

steps.whatToRemember: אבא שאול says יבום is allowed only for the מצוה. The חכמים say יבום is valid whatever his reason.

phrases.english: And the Sages say:
"Her brother-in-law shall come upon her" — in any case.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא by giving the view that opposes אבא שאול.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: יבום is valid and proper even when it is not done purely for the מצוה.

steps.title: Who taught the ברייתא that calls יבום a 'מצוה'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא: she was permitted, then forbidden, then permitted again. Does she go back to her first permission? No — the פסוק says it is a 'מצוה'. The גמרא asks which תנא this follows.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who taught what the רבנן taught: 'Her יבם shall come upon her' — it is a מצוה. At first she was permitted to him. Then she became forbidden. Then she became permitted again. You might think she goes back to her first permission. So the פסוק says, 'Her יבם shall come upon her' — a מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא and asks which תנא it follows. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא describes three stages: permitted before she married his brother, forbidden during the marriage, and permitted again after his brother died. It stresses that the new permission is not the same as the old one. Instead it is a 'מצוה'. The question is whose view needs that point.

keyTerms.meaning: Who is the תנא (which Sage) behind this teaching?
Included among the women permitted to him
'The פסוק teaches' — introduces the proof from a פסוק

phrases.english: Who taught this, which the Rabbis taught:
"Her brother-in-law shall come upon her" — it is a מצוה!
For at first she was among those permitted to him.
She became forbidden, and then became permitted again,
one might think she returns to her original permission —
so the verse says: "Her brother-in-law shall come upon her" — a מצוה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that the מחלוקת of אבא שאול and the חכמים is known, the גמרא looks for which side this ברייתא follows.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא is behind the ברייתא that calls יבום a 'מצוה' and says she does not return to her first permission?

steps.title: רבי יצחק בר אבדימי: It is אבא שאול
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק בר אבדימי answers that this ברייתא follows אבא שאול.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who is the תנא? רבי יצחק בר אבדימי said: It is אבא שאול.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats the question and gives the answer: the ברייתא follows אבא שאול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On this reading, the ברייתא's point is that the new permission is only 'for a מצוה', which fits אבא שאול and not the חכמים, who allow him to marry her for any reason. The next step shows how the ברייתא reads according to אבא שאול.

keyTerms.meaning: The אמורא who identifies the תנא of the ברייתא
'It is אבא שאול' — this ברייתא follows his view

phrases.english: Who is the תנא?
רבי יצחק בר אבדימי said:
It is אבא שאול.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן תַּנָּא? אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק בַּר אַבְדִּימִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 25.

steps.title: Reading the ברייתא as אבא שאול: before, any reason was fine
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק בר אבדימי explains the ברייתא: at first she was a fully permitted woman. He could marry her for her beauty or for married life.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is what it means: 'Her יבם shall come upon her' — for a מצוה. At first she was among the women permitted to him. If he wanted, he could marry her for her beauty. If he wanted, he could marry her for married life.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק בר אבדימי starts to read the ברייתא through אבא שאול's eyes. He explains what 'her first permission' really meant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'her first permission' now get a clear meaning. Before she married his brother, she was like any other single woman, so any reason for marrying her was fine. This sets up the contrast in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And this is what it is saying' — introduces an explanation of a text

phrases.english: And this is what it is saying:
"Her brother-in-law shall come upon her" — only for a מצוה.
For at first she was among those permitted to him.
If he wanted to, for her beauty — he could marry her;
if he wanted to, for married life — he could marry her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 26's answer by reading the ברייתא's wording according to אבא שאול.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'Her first permission' means the time when he could marry her for any reason at all.

steps.title: Now יבום is permitted only for the מצוה
steps.stepSummary: After she became forbidden and then permitted again, she does not go back to that open permission. The פסוק allows her only for the מצוה, just as אבא שאול holds.
steps.simpleTranslation: She became forbidden, then became permitted again. You might think she goes back to her first permission. So the פסוק says, 'Her יבם shall come upon her' — for the מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The explanation ends. The new permission after the brother's death holds only when יבום is done for the מצוה. This matches אבא שאול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא contrasts two kinds of permission. The first was open, for any reason. The second is limited, only 'for the מצוה'. That limit is exactly אבא שאול's view, so the ברייתא is his.

keyTerms.meaning: She went back and became permitted again
For the sake of the מצוה — only for that

steps.whatToRemember: According to אבא שאול, a יבמה is not permitted like a regular woman. She is permitted only for the מצוה of יבום. That is why the earlier generations put חליצה first.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains how the earlier and later practices in steps 19–22 fit together. Following אבא שאול leads to putting חליצה first, while following the רבנן allows יבום first.

phrases.english: She became forbidden, then became permitted again.
One might think she returns to her original permission —
so the verse says: "Her brother-in-law shall come upon her" — for the מצוה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the reading begun in step 27 by contrasting the new, limited permission with the old, open one.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The ברייתא follows אבא שאול. After the brother's death, the יבמה is permitted only for the מצוה, not for any reason as before.

steps.title: רבא: the ברייתא can fit the רבנן too
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the ברייתא does not have to follow אבא שאול. He starts reading it again: before she married his brother, she was a permitted woman, and he could marry her or not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: You can even say this ברייתא follows the רבנן. This is what it means: 'Her יבם shall come upon her' teaches that it is a מצוה. At first she was a permitted woman to him. If he wanted, he could marry her, and if he wanted, he did not have to.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a different answer from רבי יצחק בר אבדימי. He says the ברייתא can match the רבנן, and he begins explaining it from the start.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יצחק בר אבדימי read 'מצוה' the way אבא שאול does: he may marry her only for the מצוה‎. רבא keeps the same first stage, when she was simply permitted and he could take her or leave her. He is getting ready to give 'מצוה' a different meaning that the רבנן can accept.

keyTerms.meaning: You can even say it follows the רבנן (the majority view)
And this is what it means

phrases.english: Rava said: You can even say it follows the Rabbis,
and this is what it is saying:
'Her brother-in-law shall come upon her': it is a מצוה.
For at first she was among the permitted women.
If he wished, he married her; if he wished, he did not marry her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second answer to the question in step 25, against רבי יצחק בר אבדימי's answer that the ברייתא follows אבא שאול.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא does the ברייתא follow?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It can follow even the רבנן, if 'מצוה' is read differently.

steps.title: רבא continues: the 'might think' of the ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: רבא continues his reading. She became forbidden when she married his brother, and permitted again when the brother died. We might think she goes back to her original free status.
steps.simpleTranslation: She became forbidden, then became permitted again. You might think she goes back to her first permission: if he wants, he marries her, and if he wants, he does not.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא keeps reading the ברייתא's 'you might think' step the way it is written. The גמרא is about to question this line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא's wording suggests that, after the brother dies, the יבם is as free as he was at the start, so he can take her or simply not. This sets up the question in the next step.

phrases.english: She became forbidden, then became permitted again.
One might think she returns to her first permission:
if he wishes, he marries her; if he wishes, he does not marry her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבא's reading of the ברייתא from the first stage to the 'might think' stage.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ברייתא's 'might think' is that she goes back to full freedom of choice.

steps.title: Can he really just not marry her?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: how can he simply choose not to marry her? She is tied to him by the bond of יבום. Can she go free with nothing done?
steps.simpleTranslation: 'If he wishes, he does not marry her'? But she is tied to him! Should she go free for nothing?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops and questions the wording of the 'might think' line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once a woman falls to יבום, she is bound to the יבם. She cannot leave that bond without יבום or חליצה. So it makes no sense, even as a 'might think', that he could just do nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: She is tied to him (the bond of יבום)

phrases.english: 'If he wishes, he does not marry her'?
But she is tied to him!
Should she go free for nothing?
phrases.notes: He means without יבום or חליצה.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָצָה אֵינוֹ כּוֹנְסָהּ? הָא אֲגִידָה בֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the last line of step 30.
steps.kashyaTarget: The phrase 'רצה אינו כונסה' in the ברייתא's 'might think'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A יבמה is bound to the יבם and needs יבום or חליצה to be released, so 'not marrying her' and doing nothing is not a real choice.

steps.title: Correct the wording: the choice is between יבום and חליצה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא changes the wording: we might think he may choose between יבום and חליצה equally. The פסוק teaches that יבום is the מצוה, so it comes first.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say this: if he wishes, he marries her; if he wishes, he does חליצה with her. So the פסוק says, 'Her יבם shall come upon her': it is a מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the ברייתא's wording. Then it finishes רבא's reading: 'מצוה' means יבום is preferred over חליצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the 'might think' is that יבום and חליצה are equal options. The פסוק's word 'מצוה' teaches that יבום is the better choice. This is the רבנן's view, so the ברייתא no longer needs אבא שאול.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, say this (the wording is corrected)

steps.confusionAlert: The same word 'מצוה' means different things in the two answers. For רבי יצחק בר אבדימי (like אבא שאול), it means he may marry her only for the מצוה. For רבא, it means יבום is better than חליצה.
steps.whatToRemember: רבא: the ברייתא fits the רבנן. 'מצוה' teaches that יבום comes before חליצה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the ברייתא does not prove the הלכה follows אבא שאול. The רבנן can also explain it.

phrases.english: Rather, say:
if he wishes, he marries her; if he wishes, he performs ḥalitza with her.
Therefore the verse states: 'Her brother-in-law shall come upon her': it is a מצוה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אֵימָא: רָצָה — כּוֹנְסָהּ, רָצָה — חוֹלֵץ לָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection in step 31 by changing the wording, and finishes רבא's reading.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Correcting the wording of the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to say he could just walk away without marrying her.
steps.terutzMaskana: The choice was only ever between יבום and חליצה. The פסוק makes יבום the preferred מצוה, which matches the רבנן.

steps.title: Look at the first clause: מנחות eaten in a holy place
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns to the first clause of the same ברייתא, about eating מנחות as מצות in a holy place, to test the two explanations.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say the first clause: 'מצות shall be eaten in a holy place': it is a מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא brings the first clause of the ברייתא so it can check how each explanation handles it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא used the same 'permitted, forbidden, permitted again' pattern for מנחות, also with the word 'מצוה'. Any reading of 'מצוה' in the יבום clause must also make sense in this clause. The challenge itself comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: It shall be eaten as מצות

phrases.english: Say the first clause:
'It shall be eaten unleavened in a holy place': it is a מצוה.
phrases.notes: ויקרא 6:9. This is about the כהנים eating the מנחה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the יבום clause to the first clause of the ברייתא, to test both רבי יצחק בר אבדימי's and רבא's readings.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How do the two readings of 'מצוה' work in the first clause about מנחות?
